topics.title: Tiny Tim’s ‘Elvis Through the Tulips’? Radio Interview
topics.summary: During a radio interview with Howard Stern, Tiny Tim discusses his fascination with Elvis Presley and expresses interest in participating in 'Naked Jeopardy.' He shares anecdotes about his unusual diet of aunt Millie’s spaghetti sauce and sunflower seeds while discussing musical influences like classic rock songs.

topics.title: Tiny Tim and Nancy Culp Campaign Chaos
topics.summary: During the broadcast, hosts discuss Tiny Tim’s nervousness while simultaneously dissecting Nancy Culp's failed congressional campaign. The conversation veers into bizarre tangents involving drug use, wardrobe choices, political commentary – including an unexpected mention of Michael Benedict Arnold – and a critique of Barbara Bush’s appearance.

topics.title: Hollywood Mishaps and Residuals
topics.summary: During a radio discussion, the host recounts conflicts with Buddy Ebsen and Sharon Tate over financial issues related to residuals from ‘The Beverly Hillbillies’ and later projects like ‘Pee-wee’s Playhouse.’ He discusses personal anecdotes including Jane Arden's career and his own experiences in Hollywood, touching on failed movie roles and a fondness for palm springs.

topics.title: Stern Details Wife’s Massage Appointment
topics.summary: Howard Stern recounts his wife arranging a massage from a male friend, leading to concerns about privacy and inappropriate behavior. His wife wore shorts during the session while the masseuse made casual observations, causing Stern discomfort over potential unwanted attention and her revealing attire.

topics.title: Massage Preferences and Smoking Secrets Revealed
topics.summary: The conversation centers on a man’s preference for female massage therapists, expressing discomfort with male touch. Later, Fred Norris reveals his year-long attempt to quit smoking while admitting to secretly continuing throughout that time, alongside an admiration of Holly.

topics.title: Fred’s Smoking Secret
topics.summary: During a conversation, several individuals express frustration with Fred's continued smoking habit despite attempts to quit. He had been secretly lighting cigarettes for over a year while hiding them from the group, leading to accusations of deception and highlighting an uncomfortable dynamic within their interactions.
